data.title: Ares Considers Minority Stake in Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners
data.description:
Ares Management Corp. is exploring a purchase of a minority stake in Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, according to Bloomberg.

The potential deal would mark the latest high-profile expansion by the private markets firm into the infrastructure sector.

data.title: STOCKS | SpaceX Weight in Nasdaq 100 to Rise to 2.82%
data.description:
SpaceX's weight in the Nasdaq 100 index will rise to 2.82% when the index's quarterly rebalancing takes effect next Monday, up from about 1.28% now. According to Sina Finance, the final figure, calculated from Friday's closing price, matches the preliminary weight previously announced by the index compiler.

SpaceX's weight has been relatively low since it was added to the index in July, when most of the company's shares were still locked up and unavailable for public trading. Even after Nasdaq changed its rules to allow newly listed large-cap stocks to enter the index more quickly and removed the requirement that at least 10% of a company's shares be freely tradable, that factor still weighed on its index weight.

The expected increase will begin to narrow that gap. By market capitalization, SpaceX is the seventh-largest company in the Nasdaq 100, with a market value above $2 trillion, but by index weight it does not even rank in the top 20.

The higher weight matters because passive funds tied to the benchmark must adjust their holdings accordingly. Those funds include the $482 billion Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1, known as QQQ, one of the largest ETFs. More than 200 investment products worldwide track the Nasdaq 100, with assets under management exceeding $800 billion.

The Nasdaq 100 tracks large nonfinancial companies listed on the Nasdaq market. There is no minimum market-cap requirement for inclusion, but companies must have average daily trading volume of at least 200,000 shares and meet other conditions.

Edward Yin of Macquarie Group said recent index rebalancing events have taken on greater significance amid multiple market drivers. He said the adjustment is taking place against a more volatile macro backdrop, citing geopolitical tensions involving Iran, persistent inflation concerns, renewed tariff uncertainty, interest-rate moves, and continued volatility in artificial intelligence and technology stocks.

data.title: Circle's Arc Launches Facilitator Service for x402 Developer Payments
data.description: Circle's Arc public blockchain has launched agent payments through its Facilitator Service. According to Odaily, the service provides x402 developers with a hosted access path that accepts USDC and supports on-chain settlement on Arc, Base, and Polygon, without requiring a Relayer key or a separate gas fee wallet.

data.title: AI TRENDS | CoinMarketCap’s Alice Liu Says Crypto AI Capital Is Concentrating in Fewer Tokens
data.description: Crypto’s AI-token market is becoming more selective, with capital flowing into a small group of projects while hundreds of AI-labeled tokens struggle to attract meaningful participation. According to NS3.AI, CoinMarketCap’s Alice Liu said the category includes about 945 tokens worth $18.5 billion in total, but fewer than one in 10 meet both a $20 million market-cap threshold and $1 million in daily trading volume. Liu expects AI’s share of crypto capital to grow while concentrating in perhaps a dozen or two names.

data.title: Blink Says Attackers Accessed Small Number of Custodial Accounts and Withdrew Funds
data.description: Bitcoin News posted on X that attackers accessed a small number of Blink custodial accounts and withdrew funds. According to Odaily, Blink said most funds remain safe, non-custodial wallets were not affected, and it has not confirmed whether the Bitcoin payment protocol Spark, which supports several Lightning Network wallets, was the source of the security incident.

data.title: SEC Issues Innovation Exemption for On-Chain Secondary Trading of Tokenized Stocks
data.description:
Galaxy’s head of research said on X that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has issued an "innovation exemption" to create a path for on-chain secondary trading of tokenized stocks. According to Odaily, the exemption will run from September 17, 2026, to September 17, 2031, and will apply to certain tokenized securities trading venues that offer permissioned automated market makers and liquidity pools.

The venues must be deployed on public, permissionless blockchains, but trading will be limited to verified or authorized participants. Eligible tokens must correspond to actual U.S. National Market System stocks and grant the same shareholder rights as traditional shares. The exemption does not cover primary issuance, synthetic exposure, or products that do not carry legal or beneficial rights to the underlying stock. Galaxy said it is studying next steps for enabling on-chain secondary trading of GLXY.

data.title: Hut 8 Co-Founder Warns AI Growth Could Pose Systemic Risks
data.description:
Hut 8 co-founder Marc van der Chijs warned in a CoinDesk interview that intense competition between companies and nations is accelerating artificial intelligence development beyond human control, creating potential systemic risks for financial systems and critical infrastructure. According to ChainCatcher, he said the situation has already been lost to control and that systemic damage or catastrophic failure may be nearly unavoidable before real international guardrails are established.

Van der Chijs said AI and robotics could eventually replace 90% to 95% of existing jobs and sharply reduce the cost of goods and services, forcing governments to seek new revenue sources such as taxes on robots or AI use. He also said AI could expose vulnerabilities in traditional banking software and weaken confidence in institutions that rely on interconnected systems. In crypto, he argued that businesses built around Bitcoin, such as exchanges, may be more vulnerable than the underlying network itself.

He said he previously sold a large amount of Bitcoin to invest in AI and believes capital shifting into AI helped prevent Bitcoin from reaching his earlier $200,000 to $250,000 target. He is now reinvesting some AI profits into crypto assets through exchange-traded funds. Van der Chijs said he still views Bitcoin as the only asset worth holding for life and called Hut 8's move into AI data centers the best decision it has ever made.

data.title: Moody’s Lowers Mozambique Further Into Junk on Eurobond Restructuring Risk
data.description: Moody’s Ratings cut Mozambique’s credit assessment deeper into junk, citing increased risk that the gas-rich southeast African nation will restructure its sole eurobond, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: SAVE Borrowers Face Higher Student Loan Bills as Exit Deadline Nears
data.description:
According to CNBC, many federal student loan borrowers could see their monthly payments double or triple in the coming weeks if they do not leave the now-defunct Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, repayment plan. The Trump administration told borrowers earlier this year that they would have about 90 days to move to another program, and for some borrowers that window began July 1, making the earliest deadline Sept. 29.

Servicers are sending notices in waves, so many borrowers have more time. More than 6.9 million borrowers were still enrolled in SAVE as of March, with an average debt of about $55,000, according to an analysis by higher education expert Mark Kantrowitz. If borrowers do not choose another repayment plan within 90 days of notification, they will be moved into either the Standard Repayment Plan or the new Tiered Standard Plan, which launched July 1. Kantrowitz said payments for some borrowers could double or triple.

The Biden administration-era SAVE plan offered very low monthly payments, but it was overturned by Republican-led legal challenges and legislation. Many enrollees have not made a payment in more than two years while lawsuits played out, and their balances have grown with interest. Borrowers can apply for another income-driven repayment plan through studentaid.gov or their servicer's website, but the Education Department is still working through a backlog of more than 530,000 pending income-driven repayment applications as of the end of April, according to a May court filing.

A new income-driven option, the Repayment Assistance Plan, or RAP, launched in July and caps monthly payments at 1% to 10% of earnings, with loan forgiveness after 30 years. An analysis provided to CNBC by student loan advisory platform Summer found that a two-person household earning just over $50,000 with $60,000 in student debt at a 6.8% interest rate would owe $690 a month under the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan, compared with $158 under RAP.

data.title: AI | MBA Programs Adapt as Stanford Keeps Top Spot in Bloomberg Businessweek Rankings
data.description:
Stanford Graduate School of Business remained No. 1 in Bloomberg Businessweek’s US MBA rankings, with strong marks in compensation, networking and entrepreneurship, according to Bloomberg.

Bloomberg Businessweek Senior Editor Dimitra Kessenides said business schools are also testing AI in teaching, case studies and career preparation as they work to give graduates the skills employers increasingly expect.

data.title: STOCKS | Used-Car Prices Surge as $30,000 Buys Toyota With 90,000 Miles
data.description:
Used-car prices have climbed to the point where $30,000 can buy a Toyota with 90,000 miles, according to Bloomberg.

Benjamin Young’s recent experience on a used-car lot illustrates how severe America’s affordability crisis has become.

data.title: Diesel Prices Add Pressure on Fed Rate Path
data.description:
The Federal Reserve unanimously raised its benchmark rate by a quarter point as policymakers continue to face inflation above target and geopolitical uncertainty, according to Bloomberg.

Merrill and Bank of America Head of CIO Market Strategy Joe Quinlan told Bloomberg This Weekend hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that elevated diesel prices are a particular concern for businesses and could keep pressure on the Fed to raise rates further.

data.title: U.S. Central Command Says Main Strait of Hormuz Channel Has Been Cleared of Mines
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, U.S. Central Command Commander Brad Cooper said in a video on September 19 that the main shipping channel in the Strait of Hormuz has been cleared of mines, with thousands of ships having passed through, more than 1 billion barrels of crude oil shipped through the strait by Gulf partners, and the volume of crude oil, cargo and liquefied natural gas transported through the region over the past two weeks reaching the highest level in the past six months.

data.title: Hyperliquid Burns 26,310 HYPE Tokens in 24 Hours, Raising Total Burned Supply to 48.76 Million
data.description:
Hyperliquid burned 26,310 HYPE tokens over the past 24 hours, with a weighted average purchase price of $91.86, according to OnchainLens monitoring. According to BlockBeats On-chain Detection, the total burned amount of HYPE has reached 48.76 million tokens, representing 4.88% of the maximum supply.

The company also generated $64.34 million in revenue over the past 30 days, bringing cumulative revenue to $1.26 billion.

data.title: Ripple Says Asset Managers Are Preparing to Use XRP Ledger Batch V1.1
data.description:
Ripple said asset managers and other commercial projects are preparing to use Batch V1.1, an XRP Ledger feature that can combine up to eight linked transactions into one operation. According to NS3.AI, the rebuilt upgrade is expected to activate shortly after Sept. 29 if validator support remains above 80 percent.

Ripple said the redesign and security review followed a critical flaw in the original version. The company said the feature is intended for use by asset managers and other commercial projects once it goes live.

data.title: Richard Galvin Says Bitcoin and Crypto May Near a Cyclical Turning Point
data.description:
Hedge fund manager Richard Galvin said Bitcoin and the broader cryptocurrency market may be approaching a major cyclical turning point, though he warned prices could still fall further before a sustained recovery. According to NS3.AI, depressed trading activity, tokenization and artificial intelligence could help drive the next expansion.

Galvin also pointed to recent gains in specific tokens, with Zcash rising 22% over the week and Hyperliquid advancing 11% as privacy assets and on-chain trading attracted attention.

data.title: Musk Says X Usage Reaches All-Time High
data.description: U.S. President Donald Trump was not mentioned in this report. According to ChainCatcher, Elon Musk said X platform usage has reached an all-time high.

data.title: S&P 500 Falls 0.1% for the Week as Boeing, Bank of America, Wynn Resorts Turn Oversold
data.description: According to CNBC, the S&P 500 fell 0.1% for the week and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.7%, leaving several stocks in oversold territory after a volatile stretch for markets. Boeing had an RSI of 25 after shares slipped more than 5% when CEO Kelly Ortberg said production of the company's 737 Max was taking longer than expected to stabilize. Bank of America fell into oversold territory with an RSI of 28 after shares slid 8% this week, as Chief Executive Brian Moynihan said investment banking fees for the third quarter are expected to fall more than 10%. Wynn Resorts was the most oversold stock on the list with an RSI of 17 after shares fell more than 5% to a new 52-week low just above $81. Las Vegas Sands, Carrier Global and TransDigm were also oversold. On the other side of the ledger, Marathon Petroleum had an RSI of 87 and topped the overbought list after shares rose more than 7% to a record high of $428. The stock has gained 161% year to date, while Valero Energy and Phillips 66 also appeared on the overbought list.

data.title: Crypto News | Bitcoin Tops Tesla at $1.63T — BOJ Hikes but Yen Falls, Morgan Stanley ETF Runs 20 Sessions Without an Outflow, Altcoin ETF Race Heats Up
data.description: Bitcoin's market cap crossed $1.63T, surpassing Tesla and returning to the top 15 global assets — up 5% over 24 hours. The BOJ hiked to a 31-year high of 1.25% but the yen fell to 157.80 anyway as two board members dissented and guidance stayed vague — keeping carry trade funding cheap and removing the risk-off signal a hike was supposed to deliver. Morgan Stanley's MSBT ran 20 consecutive sessions without a single outflow day through one of the most volatile months of the year. XRP exchange reserves hit a 7-year low. The 21Shares Injective ETF amended its S-1, joining the growing queue of altcoin ETF filings.Bitcoin Market Cap Tops Tesla, Returns to Top 15 Global AssetsBitcoin's market cap reached $1.63T — surpassing Tesla's $1.438T (closed Friday at $364.27, -0.53%) — and returning to the top 15 global assets. The 5% 24-hour gain came against a week that delivered the Fed's first hike since July 2023, a CLARITY Act failure, oil at $106, and a BOJ hike. Blockware's Mitchell Askew's seller exhaustion read holds: Bitcoin is down just 1.5% in September — its historically worst month — after absorbing four simultaneous macro headwinds. Above price, 8% of supply was acquired between $80,000-$82,000 with the 50-week moving average at $81,081 — the ceiling that hasn't been cleared since September 4.﻿ Morgan Stanley's Bitcoin ETF Has Gone 20 Sessions Without an Outflow DayMSBT accumulated ~$51.5M over 20 consecutive sessions without a single redemption day — roughly $2.6M per session. The amount is a fraction of the $99.5B complex, but the consistency through a month that included a $731M single-day inflow, a $450M single-day outflow, and the CLARITY Act collapse is the signal. Steady, schedule-driven flows through volatility point to advisory or model-driven allocation rather than discretionary trading — consistent with Morgan Stanley's wealth management distribution. Bitcoin ETFs remain ~$1B negative year-to-date despite August's $3.52B surge, with the fee gap between GBTC's 1.50% and IBIT's 0.25% still the primary driver of complex-wide flow composition.﻿The Yen Fell 1.2% to 157.80 in the Session After the BOJ Raised RatesThe BOJ hiked to 1.25% by a 7-2 vote — two dovish dissenters (Asada, Sato) — and the yen promptly fell to 157.80 rather than strengthening. SMBC's Hirofumi Suzuki: "The two dissenting votes conveyed a dovish impression and tempered expectations for further hikes." A currency weakening on a rate hike means the hike was fully priced and/or read as insufficient. For crypto, yen weakness at 157.80 keeps carry trade funding cheap — supportive for risk assets, opposite of what a hike typically delivers. European indices fell across the board (Euro Stoxx 50 -1.22%, FTSE -1.03%, DAX -0.94%). Silver outpaced gold 6-to-1: +2.32% to $66.47 vs gold's +0.36% to $4,364.﻿SEC Receives Amended S-1/A for 21Shares Injective ETF as Altcoin ETF Race Heats UpThe SEC received an amended S-1/A for the 21Shares Injective ETF (proposed ticker: TINJ on Nasdaq), updating an October 2025 original filing. INJ staking rewards ranged from 9.3%-13.62% annually in 2025 — a yield dimension most equity ETFs cannot match. INJ's market cap sits at ~$488M, meaning even modest ETF inflows could represent a meaningful share of float. 21Shares already offers an INJ staking ETP in Europe. The filing joins a growing queue of altcoin ETF registrations covering SOL, XRP, LTC, ADA, and DeFi tokens since spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in January 2024. Custody arrangements remain unfinalized — a detail the SEC will want resolved before any approval.﻿XRP Spot ETFs Record $5.15 Million Outflow as Exchange Reserves Hit Seven-Year LowXRP spot ETFs recorded a $5.15M outflow Thursday while remaining $9.60M positive for the week — with a 10th consecutive week of net inflows possible if Friday's data doesn't exceed that figure. More structurally significant: XRP exchange reserves fell to a 7-year low near 1.7B XRP. Low exchange reserves mean less immediately available selling inventory — the same supply squeeze dynamic that preceded Bitcoin's August breakout. CME's XRP futures share rose to 17% from 10% in mid-August as institutional positioning built on regulated venues. The CLARITY Act's failure removed the near-term legislative catalyst, but SEC and CFTC rulemaking under existing authority remains the open regulatory pathway.

data.title: Hong Kong Jails Ex-CCB (Asia) Banker For USDT Bribery Scheme
data.description: A Hong Kong court jailed former China Construction Bank (Asia) relationship manager Lam Chun-yin for four years after he took more than $470,000 in Tether (USDT) to authenticate forged bank instruments with a stated value above $1.6 billion. According to BeInCrypto, the ICAC said Lam, 32, worked in consumer banking at a Causeway Bay retail branch and was never authorized to handle letters of credit; the case involved Vesttoo Limited, Yu Po Holdings Limited and a scheme to conceal bribe payments through cryptocurrency.
